reasons: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output for a compliant finding; the rendered redline is identical to the original paragraphs, so nothing is over-flagged or improperly edited.

The cited text supports the preferred position: Section 9.6 imposes only reciprocal, ordinary late-payment interest capped at the maximum lawful rate (a time-value remedy, not a stipulated penalty), and Section 12.2(a)(i) permits Sanofi (our party) to terminate for convenience on notice alone with no early-termination or minimum fee.

Section 12.6 preserves ordinary remedies rather than fixing a sum payable by us, so no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalty exists in the cited material; deterministic checks are empty, consistent with a no-edit compliant record.

Minor: the rationale's assertion that the rule 'expressly treats' late-payment interest as non-LD overstates the playbook text, but the substantive conclusion (ordinary interest is not liquidated damages) is correct and does not affect the classification.
